answer: Reputation decays with an exponential temporal half-life, so influence must be renewed through sustained honest service rather than accumulated once. In an EigenTrust-style matrix, a freshly spawned Sybil identity has near-zero eigenvector centrality: without reciprocal, credible interactions, transitive trust cannot amplify its score enough to pass consensus. A grove of colluding accounts may mirror one another’s endorsements, but that circular signal carries little weight absent trusted paths from established peers.
